findings.title: canManage() grants manage access to users with only VIEW permission on groups
findings.body: The no-arg `canManage()` method checks `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, meaning a user with only VIEW permission on all groups will pass this check. This method is used by `requireManage()` which gates `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` (group creation). A user with only VIEW permission on groups would be able to create new top-level groups, which is a privilege escalation. The V1 implementation (`GroupPermissions.canManage()`) correctly only checks `AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS`. The fix should be to only check `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` scope, not VIEW.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, `groupResource.getId()` returns the internal authorization resource ID, not the group ID. In V2, resources are created with the group ID as their *name* (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup()` which returns `group.getId()` as the resource name). Callers of this method (e.g., `UsersResource.getUsersCount`, `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)`) expect actual group IDs. Additionally, `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` will fail to find the specific resource by name (since the auth resource ID is not the group ID), causing it to fall back to the all-groups resource type check, making per-group permission evaluation incorrect. Both usages should use `groupResource.getName()` instead of `groupResource.getId()`.

findings.title: Javadoc for canManage() incorrectly documents VIEW as sufficient for manage
findings.body: The Javadoc for `canManage()` states 'For V2 only: Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups.' This documents a privilege escalation as intended behavior. Since `canManage()` gates write operations (group creation, deletion, update), only MANAGE permission should be sufficient. The documentation should be corrected to match the expected security semantics (MANAGE only), and the implementation in `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` should be fixed accordingly.

findings.title: testManageAllGroups does not register cleanup for the group created by realmAdminClient
findings.body: In `testManageAllGroups()`, a group named 'testGroup' is created via `realmAdminClient` at line 165, but no cleanup is registered for it (unlike other tests that use `realm.cleanup().add(...)`). If the test fails after group creation, the group will persist and may affect subsequent test runs. A cleanup should be added similar to the pattern used elsewhere in the test class.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle Groups resource type, falls back to displayName which may be null
findings.body: The `getResourceName` method only handles the USERS resource type explicitly. For GROUPS resources, it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Since group resources in V2 are created with the group ID as their name and no explicit display name is set, `getDisplayName()` may return null or the raw group ID rather than the human-readable group name. This could cause UI issues when displaying resource names in the admin console.
